records.source: לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ אַל־תַּ֭שְׁחֵת לְדָוִ֣ד מִכְתָּ֑ם בְּבָרְח֥וֹ מִפְּנֵי־שָׁ֝א֗וּל בַּמְּעָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: For the director, do not destroy, of David, a miktam, when he fled from before Saul in the cave.
pieces: For the music director. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." Of David. A miktam, when he fled from Saul into the cave.

L.1: For the director: "Do not destroy." Of David. A miktam, when he fled from Saul into the cave.

R.1: For the leader of the music. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." A song of David, from the time when he ran away from Saul and hid in the cave.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: al tashcheth: "Do not destroy", probably a tune
decisions.reason: The words mean "Do not destroy". They head Psalms 57-59 and 75, and are probably the name of a tune; compare the saying in Isaiah 65:8, "Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it".

decisions.choice: miktam: a kind of psalm whose meaning is unknown
decisions.reason: As in 16:1. The word (miktam) heads Psalms 16 and 56-60. Its meaning is lost; the ancient Greek translation took it as an inscription on a stone, and others link it to a word for gold.

decisions.choice: David in the cave: 1 Samuel 22 and 24
decisions.reason: David hid from Saul in the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1) and in a cave near En-gedi, where he spared Saul's life (1 Samuel 24). The title of Psalm 142 also speaks of the cave.

decisions.choice: "Do not destroy" (L); To the tune "Do Not Destroy" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Every level translates the words, as in Psalms 58 and 59; Balanced and Readable take them as a tune name (m3).
Its meaning is unknown; Readable says only that it is a song.

records.heading: Shelter in the shadow of your wings

records.source: חָנֵּ֤נִי אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀חָנֵּ֗נִי כִּ֥י בְךָ֮ חָסָ֪יָה נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י וּבְצֵֽל־כְּנָפֶ֥יךָ אֶחְסֶ֑ה עַ֝֗ד יַעֲבֹ֥ר הַוּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me, for in you takes refuge my soul, and in [the] shadow of your wings I will take refuge until passes by destruction.
pieces: Show me grace, God, show me grace, \q for I have made {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} my refuge; \q I will shelter under the shadow of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wings \q until the time of ruin is over.

L.2: Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me, \q for in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} my soul takes refuge; \q and in the shadow of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wings I will take refuge \q until [the] destruction passes by.

R.2: God, be kind to me. Please be kind to me. \q I run to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for safety. \q I will hide under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wings until all this trouble is over.

decisions.choice: the shadow of your wings: God's protection
decisions.reason: God shelters his people as a bird covers its young (17:8; 36:8; Ruth 2:12).
The word (hawwot) is plural, "destructions": the dangers that threaten him, pictured as a storm that passes over (Isaiah 26:20).

decisions.choice: take refuge: run to God for shelter
decisions.reason: As in 7:2 and 11:1. The verb comes twice: he has taken shelter in God and will stay there.
Nefesh here is the person himself.
Readable gives the sense of the word (m2).

records.source: אֶ֭קְרָא לֵֽאלֹהִ֣ים עֶלְי֑וֹן לָ֝אֵ֗ל גֹּמֵ֥ר עָלָֽי׃
records.gloss: I call to God Most High, to God who completes for me.
pieces: I call on God Most High, \q the God who carries out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan for me.

L.3: I call to God Most High, \q to God who completes [it] for me.

R.3: I pray to the God who is above all. \q He will do everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has planned for me.

decisions.choice: who completes for me: who carries his purpose for me through
decisions.reason: The verb (gamar) means to bring to an end or complete. As in 138:8, God finishes what he has begun for his servant. The ancient Greek translation reads "who has done good to me".
As in 46:5, the title ('Elyon) names God as the highest over all.
Balanced supplies the object the verb implies (m1).

decisions.choice: the God who is above all
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title means (m2).

records.source: יִשְׁלַ֤ח מִשָּׁמַ֨יִם׀וְֽיוֹשִׁיעֵ֗נִי חֵרֵ֣ף שֹׁאֲפִ֣י סֶ֑לָה יִשְׁלַ֥ח אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים חַסְדּ֥וֹ וַאֲמִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He will send from heaven and save me; he reproaches [the one] trampling on me. Selah. God will send his loyal love and his faithfulness.
pieces: He will reach down from heaven and rescue me, \q and disgrace the one who hounds me; \q God will send forth {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithfulness. Selah

L.4: He will send from heaven and save me; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will put to shame the one who tramples on me; \q God will send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithfulness. Selah

R.4: He will send help from heaven and save me. \q He will shame the people who chase after me. \q God will send me {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promises to me. Selah

decisions.choice: he will send: love and faithfulness as messengers
decisions.reason: The first "send" has no object; the second line supplies it. God's loyal love and faithfulness are pictured as messengers sent to rescue him (43:3).

alternatives: he taunts the one who tramples on me
decisions.reason: The verb (charaf) means to reproach or taunt; here God turns the attacker's scorn back on him.

decisions.choice: the one trampling on me: the one hounding me
decisions.reason: The verb of 56:2-3.
As in 5:8 (chesed): the love that keeps faith and does not give up.
The Hebrew puts Selah in the middle of the verse, after the first line. Every level puts it at the end so that the verse reads as a whole.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: his faithful love; keep his promises
alternatives: his loyal love and his faithfulness
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed, and it gives the sense of faithfulness ('emet).

records.source: נַפְשִׁ֤י׀בְּת֥וֹךְ לְבָאִם֮ אֶשְׁכְּבָ֪ה לֹ֫הֲטִ֥ים בְּֽנֵי־אָדָ֗ם שִׁ֭נֵּיהֶם חֲנִ֣ית וְחִצִּ֑ים וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם חֶ֣רֶב חַדָּֽה׃
records.gloss: My soul [is] in [the] midst of lions; I lie down [among] devourers, [the] children of humankind; their teeth [are] a spear and arrows, and their tongue a sword sharp.
pieces: I am surrounded by lions; I must lie down among people who devour like beasts. \q Their teeth are spear points and arrows, \q their tongues a sharpened sword.

L.5: My soul [is] in the midst of lions; I lie down [among] devourers, \q the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}, whose teeth [are] spear and arrows, \q and their tongue a sharp sword.

R.5: I am surrounded by enemies who are like lions. I have to lie down among people who want to eat me alive. \q Their teeth are like spears and arrows. \q Their words cut like a sharp sword.

decisions.reason: Enemies are often pictured as lions ready to tear their prey (7:3; 22:14; 35:17).
The word (lohatim) may come from a verb meaning to devour or from one meaning to blaze. The lions are human beings, "the children of humankind".
Their words wound like spears, arrows and swords (52:4; 55:22; 59:8).
Nefesh here is the person himself.

decisions.choice: children of humankind, with "sons of men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in 11:4.

decisions.choice: enemies who are like lions; people who want to eat me alive
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean (m1, m2).

records.source: ר֣וּמָה עַל־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם אֱלֹהִ֑ים עַ֖ל כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Be exalted above the heavens, God; over all the earth your glory.
pieces: God, be lifted high above the heavens; \q let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory spread over all the earth.

L.6: Be exalted above the heavens, God; \q over all the earth [be] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory.

R.6: God, show that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are higher than the heavens! \q Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory shine over the whole earth!

decisions.reason: The prayer (rum) asks God to show his greatness by acting (21:14; 46:11).
God's glory (kavod) is the weight and splendor of his presence, seen when he acts.
This verse comes again as the last verse of the psalm (verse 12), closing both of its halves.

decisions.choice: show that you are higher than the heavens
decisions.reason: Readable says what the prayer asks (m1).

records.source: רֶ֤שֶׁת׀הֵכִ֣ינוּ לִפְעָמַי֮ כָּפַ֪ף נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י כָּר֣וּ לְפָנַ֣י שִׁיחָ֑ה נָפְל֖וּ בְתוֹכָ֣הּ סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: A net they prepared for my steps; bowed down my soul; they dug before me a pit; they have fallen into its midst. Selah.
pieces: They laid a net for my steps, and I sank down in despair; \q they hollowed out a pit ahead of me, \q and into it they fell. Selah

L.7: A net they set for my steps; my soul was bowed down; \q they dug a pit before me; \q they have fallen into the middle of it. Selah

R.7: My enemies set a trap to catch me, and I was very upset. \q They dug a hole for me to fall into, \q but they are the ones who fell into it! Selah

decisions.reason: Animals were caught in nets and in covered pits (9:16; 35:7-8).

decisions.choice: they have fallen into it: their evil turns back on them
decisions.reason: As in 7:16, the trap catches the one who set it. The past form speaks of it as certain.

decisions.choice: bowed down: bent low with distress
decisions.reason: The verb (kafaf) is used of a person bowed down by trouble (145:14).

decisions.choice: I sank down in despair (B); I was very upset (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense (m3).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: נָ֘כ֤וֹן לִבִּ֣י אֱ֭לֹהִים נָכ֣וֹן לִבִּ֑י אָ֝שִׁ֗ירָה וַאֲזַמֵּֽרָה׃
records.gloss: Steadfast [is] my heart, God, steadfast [is] my heart; I will sing and I will make music.
pieces: My heart is firm, God, my heart is firm; \q I will sing and play songs of praise.

L.8: Steadfast [is] my heart, God, steadfast [is] my heart; \q I will sing and make music.

R.8: God, my heart is calm and sure. \q I am ready to sing and to play music in praise of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.reason: The word (nakhon) is the one David prayed for in 51:12: a heart firmly fixed on God (112:7).
Verses 8-12 appear again, with small changes, as Psalm 108:2-6.

decisions.choice: make music: sing praise with instruments
decisions.reason: The verb (zamar) is to sing praise, often with instruments (verse 9).
Readable says whom the music is for.

records.source: ע֤וּרָה כְבוֹדִ֗י ע֭וּרָֽה הַנֵּ֥בֶל וְכִנּ֗וֹר אָעִ֥ירָה שָּֽׁחַר׃
records.gloss: Awake, my glory! Awake, the harp and lyre! I will awaken [the] dawn.
pieces: Rouse yourself, my soul! \q Come awake, harp and lyre! \q I will wake up the dawn.

L.9: Wake up, my glory! \q Wake up, harp and lyre! \q I will wake the dawn.

R.9: Wake up, my soul! \q Harp and lyre, wake up! \q I will be up singing before the sun rises.

alternatives: my liver (with other vowels), the seat of feeling
decisions.reason: "My glory" (kavod) is a way of speaking of one's whole inner being (16:9; 30:13). With other vowels the word means the liver, thought of as the seat of the feelings.
Two stringed instruments used in worship (33:2).

decisions.choice: wake the dawn: be up praising before sunrise
decisions.reason: Instead of the dawn waking him, he will wake the dawn with his song.
Balanced gives the sense of the word (m1).

decisions.choice: I will be up singing before the sun rises
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m3).

records.gloss: I will thank you among the peoples, Lord; I will make music to you among the nations.
pieces: Lord, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} before all peoples; \q I will sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise in every nation.

L.10: I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among the peoples, my Lord; \q I will make music to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among the nations.

R.10: Lord, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in front of people everywhere. \q I will sing songs of praise to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in every country.

decisions.choice: among the peoples: praise heard by all nations
decisions.reason: The psalmist will praise God not only in Israel but before the nations, so that they too may know him (18:50; 96:3).
The title 'Adonai means "my Lord", master; it is not the divine name.
In address, "Lord" carries the sense of "my Lord" ('Adonai); Literal keeps "my".

records.gloss: For great to [the] heavens [is] your loyal love, and to [the] clouds your faithfulness.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love towers up to the heavens, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness rises to the clouds.

L.11: For great to the heavens [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, \q and to the clouds {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness.

R.11: Your faithful love is higher than the sky. \q Your faithfulness reaches all the way to the clouds.

decisions.choice: to the heavens, to the clouds: beyond measure
decisions.reason: As in 36:6, the height of the sky is the measure of God's love (103:11).
As in 5:8 (chesed): the love that keeps faith and does not give up.
The word ('emet) means that God can be relied on to keep his word.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: ר֣וּמָה עַל־שָׁמַ֣יִם אֱלֹהִ֑ים עַ֖ל כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Be exalted above [the] heavens, God; over all the earth your glory.
pieces: God, be lifted high above the heavens; \q let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory spread over all the earth.

L.12: Be exalted above the heavens, God; \q over all the earth [be] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory.

R.12: God, show that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are higher than the heavens! \q Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory shine over the whole earth!

decisions.reason: The psalm ends as its first half ended (verse 6).
As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: show that you are higher than the heavens
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.
